evals.prompt: Our editors publish in Optimizely and then ping us on Slack because the site still shows the old copy 20 minutes later. We're on Next.js 15 App Router deployed to Optimizely frontend hosting, three instances. Can you sort out the caching properly?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a missing on-demand revalidation path, not a reason to lower the revalidate interval. Should establish the deployment target as Optimizely frontend hosting and note that three instances require a shared Redis cache handler (cacheHandler in next.config.mjs with an absolute path, cacheMaxMemorySize: 0), because the default filesystem ISR cache is per-instance. Should read references/optimizely-frontend-hosting.md. Should set up: tagged cached fetches, a webhook receiver at a route like /api/revalidate validating the x-api-key header against OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_CALLBACK_APIKEY, docId parsing in the form {contentKey}_{locale}_{status}, an uncached Graph query to resolve the content key to a URL, revalidateTag plus revalidatePath, and a CDN purge via the Cloud Platform Services edge-cache purge endpoint. Should register the webhook against ${OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_GATEWAY}/api/webhooks with Basic auth (APP_KEY:SECRET) and a filter on status Published, ideally idempotently from instrumentation.ts. Should mention filtering the _N_T_/layout tag and namespacing cache keys with OPTIMIZELY_DXP_DEPLOYMENT_ID. Should keep a long revalidate interval as a fallback.

evals.prompt: What revalidate values should I use for my content types? I have ArticlePage, LandingPage, a NavigationSettings singleton, a HeroBlock and a CtaBlock that get reused all over, and a blog index page. Next.js 16, hosted on Vercel.
evals.expected_output: Should give a per-content-type table rather than one global number, roughly: articles/landing pages ~1 hour, navigation/settings ~1 day, shared blocks ~1 hour, listing/index pages ~15 minutes. Should stress that the intervals are only a self-healing fallback and that cache tags are the real mechanism. Should explain that HeroBlock and CtaBlock have no URL of their own, so revalidatePath cannot invalidate the pages embedding them — tags are required. Should propose a consistent tag vocabulary such as optimizely:content:{key}, optimizely:type:{TypeName}, and optimizely:nav. Because the project is Next.js 16, should use 'use cache' with cacheTag/cacheLife rather than unstable_cache, and must note that revalidateTag takes a cache profile as a second argument in Next.js 16 (e.g. revalidateTag(tag, 'max')). Should note Vercel needs no custom cache handler and purges its edge automatically, and should warn about registering the webhook against the stable production domain rather than a preview URL, and about Deployment Protection blocking inbound webhooks.

evals.prompt: I added `export const revalidate = 3600` to app/[...slug]/page.tsx and set up the Optimizely Graph webhook, but nothing ever updates and I don't even see the webhook hitting my app. Self-hosted in Kubernetes with 4 pods behind an nginx ingress.
evals.expected_output: Should run a systematic diagnosis rather than guessing. Should check that the route is actually static in the next build output (● / ISR rather than ƒ Dynamic) and explain that reading headers(), cookies(), or searchParams silently opts the route out of static generation, with dynamic = 'error' to surface the opt-out at build time and isolating request-dependent parts in Suspense as the fix. Should verify the webhook is registered by GETting ${OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_GATEWAY}/api/webhooks with Basic auth, and check for duplicates or stale entries pointing at a dead hostname. Should have the user POST a synthetic payload with the x-api-key header to confirm the route returns 200, and without it to confirm 401. Should identify that 4 pods without a shared cache handler is a second, independent bug: the default filesystem cache is per-pod, so revalidation only affects the pod that received the webhook. Should point to references/portable-hosting.md and provide the plain Redis cache handler (no Azure dependencies) plus cacheHandler/cacheMaxMemorySize config. Should mention that next dev ignores cacheHandler so verification requires next build && next start, and that the _N_T_/layout tag must be filtered.

evals.prompt: Write me the revalidation webhook endpoint for our Optimizely site. Next.js 15, app router, self-hosted single container behind Cloudflare.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a POST route handler (e.g. app/api/revalidate/route.ts) with export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'. Should validate the x-api-key header against OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_CALLBACK_APIKEY and return 401 otherwise. Should ignore non-'doc' subjects and non-updated/expired/deleted actions by returning 200 with a skipped flag, explaining that non-2xx responses cause Graph retry storms. Should parse docId as {contentKey}_{locale}_{status}. Should resolve the content key to a URL and type via a Graph query to ${gateway}/content/v2 with Authorization: epi-single ${OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_SINGLE_KEY} and cache: 'no-store'. Should call revalidateTag for the content and type tags and revalidatePath for the resolved path with the trailing slash stripped. Should add a Cloudflare purge_cache call because revalidating Next.js does not clear the CDN, and note that purge must target the public URL. Should say a single container needs no Redis cache handler, and give the manual curl registration against /api/webhooks with the Published status filter. Should use single-argument revalidateTag since this is Next.js 15. Should handle deletes where URL resolution returns nothing, and mention Graph eventual consistency.
